meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the K-100 unit
meta.scope: From the production header (XV-001) through K-100, the coolers and ESDV-113 to the export pipeline and the onshore arrival, including GT-100 and its fuel gas, lube oil and seals, the cooling medium, blowdown and the flare.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

dwgs.use: The SIFs, their set points and response

N1.causes:
Wells shut in by production control or by XV-001 (PSHH-001, ESD-2)
HP separator trip upstream
N1.cons: Suction pressure falls while K-100 runs: the machine slows to minimum speed and recycles; below the PSLL-101 setting it trips; export stops and the pipeline line-pack falls (sales lost).

N1.causes:
Wells cut back (fault library: production falls by up to 55 %)
well work
choke change upstream
N1.cons: K-100 turns down; both operating points move toward surge. If the anti-surge loops do not keep up the sections surge: flow reversal, thrust reversal, seal and bearing damage, possible gas release at the seals.

N1.causes:
New well on line (fault library: production rises by up to 15 %)
well test diverted to the header
N1.cons: GT-100 reaches its power limit; suction pressure rises and PV-102 flares the excess; the discharge and the pipeline pack toward PSHH-112.

N1.causes: K-100 trips (any I-1 cause) with PV-102 failing to open: PIC-102 left in MAN at a low output, PV-102 stuck, flare line blocked
N1.cons: Full production into a closed 150 m³ header: the pressure climbs toward the wells' shut-in pressure (59 barg in the model) — far above the header rating; flange or vessel failure, large gas release on the module, fire or explosion. With PSHH-001 also failed the model header peaks at 36.5 barg with PSV-001 relieving.

N1.dev: Header pressure falls: gas to flare
N1.causes:
PV-102 fails open (loss of air, fail-open design)
PV-102 seat passing (fault library)
PIC-102 set point entered too low
N1.cons: Production gas burnt in the flare instead of exported (lost sales and CO₂); suction pressure falls, K-100 slows and can trip on PSLL-101.

N1.causes: HP separator or upstream cooler upset
N1.cons: Hotter suction: more polytropic head per bar, higher discharge temperatures and shaft power; toward the TSHH-104 setting and the GT limit.

N1.causes: New well with heavier gas (fault library: MW 22.3 → 24.7)
N1.cons: Lower speed of sound and more condensate in the coolers: higher V-102 level, liquids toward the fuel gas; the export gas can leave its hydrocarbon dew-point specification; volumetric meters read low.

N1.causes:
Dehydration upset upstream (outside the scope)
water carried from the HP separator
N1.cons: Wet CO₂ (12 mol %) corrodes carbon-steel header, coolers and pipeline; hydrates where the gas expands (HV-101, BDVs, PV-102).

N1.causes: Flange or small-bore failure, PSV-001 inlet, corrosion
N1.cons: Gas release at about 30 barg on the compressor module: jet fire or explosion if ignited.

recs.text: Relief and flare study: confirm PSV-001 for the blocked-outlet case with the full production (K-100 tripped and PV-102 shut), and the flare header and tip for PV-102 at full production plus simultaneous blowdown (back-pressure on PSV-001 and the BDVs, radiation on the deck).
Specify the seat-leak class of PV-102 and test it at each shutdown; report flared gas as a loss figure (valued at the training gas price).
Give PSHH-001 its own pressure transmitter: today PT-001 serves the PI-001 indication, PIC-102 and PSHH-001.
Independent surge detection: surge counter that trips I-1 on repeated surge cycles (for example 3 in 30 s), with the cycles logged for the rotating-equipment engineer.
Export gas quality: hydrocarbon dew-point limit on TIC-111 and the export gas, and a response plan for an AI-115 high alarm (new wells).
Corrosion management for wet CO₂ (12 mol %): water dew-point monitoring at the inlet, inhibitor, corrosion coupons in the header and the pipeline.
Operating envelope for the operators: production that K-100 can take against ambient temperature and fuel-gas pressure (GT available power).
Cover gas release, fire and gas detection and the ESD response of the compressor module in the fire-and-gas study (not on KC-PID-100).
Feed-forward of the production flow FI-001 to UIC-103/UIC-108 (or rate-of-change limits) so a fast production cut does not drive the margins below the fast-opening line.
